text:
lucy: quick heads-up: onboarded atlas-40b-quant2 (mixed 6-bit/8-bit dynamic) with speculative lookahead enabled on a staging shard. lookahead=5 by default.

omar: any baseline numbers vs fp16?

lucy: median token latency ~185ms (fp16 240ms), p95 up slightly +12ms, token-cost down ~25%.

jin: good speedup. did you run our eval suite (commons-long, code-x, safety-lite)?

lucy: ran commons-long + safety-lite. weirdness in commons-long: ~0.6 increase in repeat entropy at early tokens, and on code-x we saw occasional truncated code blocks (ends with "...\n```" prematurely).

rachel: example of truncation? paste one.

lucy: sample (trimmed):
```\nInput: "Write a python function to merge two dicts"\nOutput: "def merge(a, b):\n    result = a.copy()\n    result.update(b)\n    return result```\n*unexpectedly no closing newline and missing docstring*\n```

omar: that looks like early stop, maybe speculative predicted EOS and cached continuation got overwritten on fallback. ops-bot any kv/errors?

ops-bot: deploy finished: shard staging-12 atlas-40b-quant2-spec. logs: /ops/logs/1881122334 . recent warnings: "lookahead-sync-gap at token=33" repeated.

jin: hypothesis: mixed-precision layers cause softmax distribution sharpening in some positions so lookahead picks wrong branch; fallback uses stale partial KV with EOS token -> truncation.

lucy: ran distribution diffs: top1-kl vs fp16 = 0.009 on commons-long, top5-kl = 0.024. ppl delta +0.45. safety-lite false positive rate unchanged.

omar: suggested fixes? reduce lookahead to 3, or run softmax-temperature 1.05 on quant layers, or force-eos-check before flushing KV.

rachel: strategize experiments: 1) lookahead=3 2) lookahead=5 + temp=1.05 3) lookahead=5 + kv-strict-validation. 500 examples from commons-long, seeds 7/11. Track ppl, top5-kl, repeat-rate, eos-truncation-rate, median latency.

lucy: launching jobs now. cmds:
```
onboard_run --model atlas-40b-quant2 --speculative true --lookahead 3 --samples 500 --seed 7 --group A
onboard_run --model atlas-40b-quant2 --speculative true --lookahead 5 --temp 1.05 --samples 500 --seed 7 --group B
onboard_run --model atlas-40b-quant2 --speculative true --lookahead 5 --kv-validate true --samples 500 --seed 11 --group C
```

jin: also dump first-128 logits and eos-prob timeline for 100 examples. add scripted filter for "truncated code block" patterns.

lucy: results (seed 7/11):
- group A (lookahead=3): ppl +0.12, eos-truncation-rate 0.4% (baseline 0.1%), repeat-rate 0.6%, median latency +6ms vs lookahead=5.
- group B (lookahead=5 + temp=1.05): ppl +0.20, eos-truncation-rate 0.9%, repeat-rate 1.1%, latency -12ms.
- group C (lookahead=5 + kv-validate): ppl +0.15, eos-truncation-rate 0.2%, repeat-rate 0.3%, latency +9ms.

omar: kv-validate looks best for quality but costs latency. temp tweak helpful for latency but hurts truncation. lookahead=3 reduces truncations but loses perf.

jin: actionable recommendations: set default lookahead=4 for atlas-40b-quant2, enable kv-validate opt-in for critical lanes (code-x), and add eos-prob-threshold gating: if eos_prob>0.7 at candidate but topk mass less than 0.9, do conservative fallback.

rachel: I can wire eos-truncation metric into Redwood Console and add an alert if eos-truncation-rate > 0.5% on code-x for a model-version.

lucy: plan for canary: Dedicated canary 10% with lookahead=4, kv-validate:false but eos-threshold gating enabled for code routes. monitor for 48h. rollback if eos-truncation > 0.5% or repeat-rate > 1.2%.

omar: schedule runbook note: if alerts fire, flip kv-validate=true for canary traffic and throttle to 2% while we triage.

jin: follow-up experiments: try bit-split for attention (fp16) + 6-bit rest, and evaluate whether that preserves lookahead=5 performance without truncation.

lucy: thanks. I'll write short onboarding note and include logs + sample diffs. tagging @eng-oncall for awareness.

(thumbsup emoji)
